The REST module calls `PatientService.getAllergies` in one resource class, `PatientAllergyResource2_0`, which backs the `/ws/rest/v1` allergy sub-resource under patients. Three of its methods call it, and the controller test exercises all three. Nothing else in `omod/src/main` calls it.

**Production callers (best first):**

1. `doGetAll(Patient, RequestContext)` (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs2_0/PatientAllergyResource2_0.java:165-183`). This is the GET `/patient/{uuid}/allergy` path. It branches on `getAllergyStatus()` (UNKNOWN → 204, NO_KNOWN_ALLERGIES → empty list, SEE_LIST → list). A change to the return value, status semantics, or exceptions would change the GET response directly.
2. `put(String, SimpleObject, RequestContext)` (`.../PatientAllergyResource2_0.java:294-313`). It calls `getAllergies(patient)` at line 305, checks `isEmpty()`, then calls `confirmNoKnownAllergies()` and `setAllergies`. It is the PUT path that marks a patient as "no known allergies". It would be affected if `getAllergies` stopped returning an empty `Allergies` object for patients with none, or if its privilege checks changed.
3. `delete(String, String, String, RequestContext)` (`.../PatientAllergyResource2_0.java:211-227`). On DELETE `/patient/{uuid}/allergy/` it fetches all allergies at line 222 and voids each one. A change to what the call returns would change which allergies get voided.
